matt_dev: Heads-up — customer reports batch rerank returning scores that don't line up with per-query candidate ordering. They say it only happens when some queries have an empty candidate list. Repro attached.

samir_support: Can you paste the exact request body they sent?

matt_dev: Sure, trimmed example they used (they POST to /v1/rerank/batch with gzip):
```json
{
  \"requests\": [
    { \"query\": \"q1\", \"candidates\": [\"a\", \"b\"] },
    { \"query\": \"q2\", \"candidates\": [] },
    { \"query\": \"q3\", \"candidates\": [\"x\", \"y\"] }
  ]
}
```
Headers: Content-Type: application/octet-stream (they said CSV-style encoder + gzip), Authorization: Bearer <token>

jess_eng: That pattern looks familiar — our CSV/flattening serializer currently omits the explicit empty-list marker when compressing sequences, and our per-query offsets are inferred from separators rather than authoritative counts. If a query has zero candidates we end up shifting subsequent offsets left by one.

ingrid_oncall: Customer logs show this on our side: 
```
request_id=req_0abc rerank.batch: flattened_candidates=4 per_query_counts=[2,0,2] computed_offsets=[0,2,4]
response_meta=per_query_offsets=[0,2,4]
```
But client expects offsets like [0,2,2,4] (i.e., an explicit zero-length slot), so the alignment is off.

samir_support: For an immediate workaround, ask them to either: 1) switch to JSONL mode (each request line contains its own candidates array) or 2) include an explicit per_query_counts header with counts so server uses counts instead of separators. Also recommend they avoid the CSV encoder for now if any query can be empty.

matt_dev: Filed internal issue RL-4523 with repro steps and attached their gzipped payload. Minimal repro script included. Patch suggestion: ensure the serializer writes an explicit zero-length delimiter token when candidates==[] and compute offsets from counts array instead of separator positions.

rerank-bot: Incident created: INC-2026; severity=low; owner=jess_eng; linked_issue=RL-4523; eta_patch_deploy=2024-11-05

jess_eng: I added a unit test that simulates [2,0,2] counts and checks offsets; failing on master. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/1234 — it changes the CSV encoder to emit a \"0\"-length marker and forces offsets to be derived from counts. Will run staging runbook.

samir_support: I'll update the customer with the workaround and ask for a sample of their gzipped payload (to reproduce exactly). Also confirmed billing unaffected — this is purely formatting alignment.

ingrid_oncall: If they need an urgent hotfix, we can roll the patch to dedicated clusters only (no downtime). Otherwise schedule full rollout after smoke tests.

matt_dev: Thanks — I'll keep this thread updated. Customer-facing note: \"If you see misaligned scores in batch-rerank and some queries have no candidates, please try JSONL or include per_query_counts; we have a fix ready to deploy.\" :thumbsup:

samir_support: Marking ticket escalated to eng and shared repro. Closing loop once PR merged + deployed.

(Conversation ended — thread will be updated after deploy.)
